title: Volume change feedback sound clips and sounds bad when rapidly changing volume
line: Changing the volume quickly no longer makes the feedback sound pop or pile up into overlapping chimes.
explanation: VolumeFeedback used to cancel the chime still playing on every volume step, and cutting the sound off made it pop. MR !424 removed the cancel so chimes overlap instead, and with quick steps two or three chimes now play on top of each other and pile up. Now a step that arrives while a chime is still playing is remembered and played once that chime ends, so only one chime plays at a time, nothing is cut off, and the last step is always heard.

commits.message:
VolumeFeedback: play one chime at a time when changing volume quickly

Cancelling the chime on every volume step made it pop, and letting the
chimes overlap instead piled them up. Now a step that comes while one is
still playing waits for it to end, and only the latest step is played.

BUG: 505885

media.caption: master: 16 quick volume steps (160 ms apart) play 16 chimes, up to 3 overlapping (recorded from the sink)
fixed: the same 16 steps play 8 chimes back to back, never overlapping, ending at the same time
master waveform: chimes run into each other
fixed waveform: one chime at a time

reviews.text: Waiting for the current chime to finish and playing only the latest pending step is a good UX direction that avoids both cancellation pops and overlapping chime pile-ups, and the recorded waveforms clearly demonstrate the improvement. However, the 20 ms QTimer polling implementation has a concrete bug: when a new step arrives in the window between the previous chime finishing and m_pendingTimer firing, play() starts the new chime immediately without stopping m_pendingTimer, causing the timer to fire milliseconds later with a stale m_pendingSinkIndex and queue an unwanted phantom chime. Additionally, configuring m_pendingTimer after the early return on driver failure and restarting the timer on every step are rough edges, and using libcanberra's completion callback (ca_context_play_full) would avoid polling altogether.
changes: Stop m_pendingTimer when playing == 0 before starting a new chime so a previously armed timer cannot fire afterward with a stale m_pendingSinkIndex and schedule a phantom extra chime.

Prefer an event-driven completion callback via ca_context_play_full (with safe QObject lifetime handling back to the main thread) instead of polling ca_context_playing() every 20 ms; or if keeping QTimer polling, avoid resetting an already-active timer on rapid steps (check !m_pendingTimer.isActive()) and configure m_pendingTimer unconditionally before the ca_context_set_driver early return.

reviews.text: Addresses both halves of the history in the right place (plasma-pa VolumeFeedback, shared by kded shortcuts, the applet slider/wheel and the KCM): no cancel, so no pops from cutting the sample (c6), and no overlap, so no pile-up on master after !424/!436 (c10/c11); the latest step is coalesced and played when the current chime ends, so the final level is always heard. The before/after recordings and waveforms clearly show 16 overlapping chimes becoming 8 sequential ones, and the 600 ms and 30 ms runs cover the edge cases; the commit text matches the patch. Minor nitpicks a maintainer might raise but that don't block: it polls ca_context_playing every 20 ms instead of using ca_context_play_full's finish callback, and with a long custom theme sound the last chime can lag by up to that sound's length; the applet slider path wasn't exercised on the rig but runs the same class.
